title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next generates corrupted Thai orthography under vLLM; the same model under llama.cpp at the same QSA budget is clean
body:
### Summary

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` under vLLM produces systematically malformed Thai: single-character substitutions, displaced tone marks and doubled combining marks. The same model at the same effective QSA budget under llama.cpp is clean — 0 defects across 130 samples versus 12–18 per 1000 Thai characters across five vLLM configurations.

This was originally reported as part of #54521 (non-determinism from `persistent_topk`). It is a **separate defect**: I have since shown non-determinism is not its cause, and that QSA block selection is not either. Splitting it out so #54521 can stay scoped to determinism.

### Environment

- 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121), `-tp 2`, aarch64, driver 580.159.03 / 580.95.05
- vLLM `0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198` (official `vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next` body)
- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `--enforce-eager`, stock `indexer_budget=2048`
- Sampling: the model card's temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20. **Greedy is not usable for a quality measurement on this model** — it degenerates even at 105 prompt tokens — so every number below is a rate over 10 samples.

### What the corruption looks like

The probe is a Thai date-countdown answer, so the same words recur with unambiguous correct forms:

| correct | observed |
|---|---|
| `ปีใหม่` | `ปีใหม้` (mai tho for mai ek) |
| `สงกรานต์` | `สงกรานตค์์`, thanthakhat detached or missing |
| `ครับ` | `ครรับ` (doubled ro rua) |
| `คริสต์ศักราช` | `คริศต์ศักราช` (so sala for so suea) |
| `เช่น` | `เชน่` (tone mark displaced past the consonant) |
| `คำนวณ` | `คานวณ` (sara am lost) |
| `อีก` | `อีีก` (doubled sara ii) |

Thai is a sensitive detector rather than a special case: it runs ~3x more tokens per character than English, with many near-identical combining-mark tokens, so a perturbation surfaces as visibly broken text instead of a harmless paraphrase.

### Evidence

Prompt-length ladder built from a real captured agent request by dropping tool definitions and truncating the system prompt; the conversation itself is never touched, so every rung asks the identical question. N=10 per cell, corrupt / informative samples:

| prompt tok | 20394 | 16006 | 13369 | 9635 | 8556 | 6490 | 4675 | 2959 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM stock | 6/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 | 9/9 | 9/10 | 10/10 | 7/9 | 7/10 |
| vLLM, no MTP | 7/10 | 7/10 | 7/10 | 9/9 | 7/10 | 6/8 | 6/9 | 6/8 |
| **llama.cpp** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** | **0/10** |

Five further rungs from 2631 down to 1720 tokens: vLLM 6–10/10, llama.cpp 0/10. **The corruption is not length-gated.**

A structural detector (stacked tone marks, doubled upper vowels, tone-then-vowel — independent of the word list above) over every sample collected:

| engine / configuration | samples | Thai chars | defects per 1k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| vLLM stock | 77 | 5981 | 16.55 |
| vLLM stock, short rungs | 113 | 9316 | 15.99 |
| vLLM without the sort patch | 78 | 6751 | 17.63 |
| vLLM `indexer_budget=8192` | 77 | 6486 | 14.96 |
| vLLM without MTP | 76 | 5737 | 12.90 |
| **llama.cpp UD-IQ4_XS** | **130** | **11085** | **0.00** |

### The llama.cpp comparison is matched, not approximate

llama.cpp build 10731, `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` UD-IQ4_XS, single GB10, `--jinja -c 32768`. It implements QSA itself and does not fall back to dense attention:

- `src/models/qwen4exp.cpp:423` — "QSA attends to a budget of whole blocks of compress_ratio tokens, plus the incomplete tail; one mean-pooled indexer key scores each block"
- `build_qsa_top_k` → `ggml_top_k(ctx0, expanded, width)` with `width = min(n_kv, indexer_top_k + r - 1)`, then the KQ mask is unmasked only at the selected cells

At the 20k rung that is **2051 attended tokens of 20343**. vLLM at stock `indexer_budget=2048` attends `k=512` blocks × `compress_ratio=4` = **2048 tokens**. Same algorithm, same budget, same ~10:1 sparsity, from GGUF metadata that is the model's own (`indexer.top_k = 2048`, `compress_ratios = [0,0,0,4,...]`, `full_attention_interval = 4`).

### Ruled out

- **QSA sparse block selection.** Density is `prompt_tokens <= indexer_budget` (the compress ratio cancels), so shortening the prompt reaches genuinely dense selection. Five dense cells — 4/8, 7/10, 9/10, 6/10, 8/10 — all corrupt at the sparse rate. Dense selection does not help.
- **Non-determinism.** A deterministic tie-break makes the real payload byte-identical across runs and leaves the Thai just as corrupt (#54521).
- **Speculative decoding.** `--speculative-config` removed: still 6–9/10 corrupt, 12.90 defects per 1k.
- **Quantization.** UD-IQ4_XS is a *coarser* quant than the FP8 used under vLLM, and the lower-precision weights are the clean ones.
- **The weights / the model / the QSA algorithm.** Clean under llama.cpp.
- Also eliminated earlier in #54521: prefix caching, chat template, `rows_per_chunk`, #53287, CUDA graphs (`--enforce-eager` throughout), the weight loader, and `indexer_budget` overrides.

### Not controlled

Two differences between the engines remain uncontrolled, and I would rather state them than argue them away.

**1. Chat template.** llama.cpp used the GGUF's built-in template; vLLM used a locally fixed jinja template. Prompt lengths differ by ~50 tokens per rung. The chat template was independently eliminated as a cause earlier in #54521, but it was not held identical across this particular comparison.

**2. Tensor parallelism.** llama.cpp ran single-GPU; vLLM ran `-tp 2`. I cannot close this on my hardware — FP8 is ~193 GiB (96.5 GiB per rank) and NVFP4 is 125.9 GiB, both above one GB10's ~121 GiB, so no vLLM variant of this model runs at `-tp 1` here.

**This is the most useful thing someone else could check:** does the Thai corruption reproduce on a single large-memory GPU at `-tp 1`, and on non-GB10 hardware? That would separate a tensor-parallel bug from something in the `qwen4exp` implementation generally.

### Reproduction

Any Thai generation task shows it; a short factual answer in Thai is enough, and it reproduces from 1720 tokens of prompt upward. Score with a stacked-mark detector (tone+tone, upper+upper, tone-then-vowel adjacency) rather than by eye — but note that detector is a **lower bound**, since it does not catch the substitution errors, which are the majority. Harness and all raw samples available on request.
